images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A slim brushed graphite shelf about the length of a forearm is mounted on a frosted acrylic back panel on a pale neutral tabletop. On it stands a neat row of ivory card binders with crisp spines and blank label windows, upright and evenly spaced. Most are clean, but the three at the right end carry a fine grey film of dust along their tops. The newest binder, in the middle, has a single acid-lime spine clip marking the current version. A graphite bookend with a chamfered edge holds the row. In front, a loose page lies front down on the tabletop, slightly curled. Fibre grain shows on each spine. The shelf is level and tidy, with only the dust out of place. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same graphite shelf sags hard at the centre, its bracket bending away from the frosted panel. The ivory binders have yellowed and warped, many pushed in at odd angles with split spines. Near-duplicates crowd the row, each a slightly different shade, and loose pages spill from their rings, frozen mid-air in a slow waterfall toward the tabletop. The acid-lime spine clip of the current binder has popped free and is tumbling downward. The graphite bookend has slid off the end and lies on its side. On the tabletop, pages from different binders have piled into overlapping, contradictory layers. Dust puffs from the falling binders, and every loose page traces back to the dip in the shelf. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. The hero object stays slightly left of centre, and the spread of the disaster runs to the right and toward the camera so its path can be traced back to the source. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Airborne paper, grains and fragments catch the key light with crisp edge highlights. Camera: 85mm lens at f/5.6, same three-quarter tabletop angle, fast shutter freezing everything mid-air. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A shallow flooded basin under an overcast sky, its calm grey water reflecting the ruins of a vast collapsed library. Giant ivory binders, swollen and yellowed, stand half submerged like leaning towers, their spines split and bleached, pages drifting in soft rafts on the surface. The building-sized graphite shelf lies snapped across the basin like a fallen bridge, and the frosted acrylic back panel has toppled behind it, clouded and cracked. Distant binder ruins fade into mist. In the midground, a slim graphite floating rack on pontoons with an acid-lime picker arm is lifting dry current pages from a raft and filing them into a short, straight row of new binders on its deck, the row neat against the wreckage. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: soft overcast late-afternoon daylight still falling from the upper left, with long soft shadows grounding the ruins and atmospheric haze fading distant forms into pale grey-green.
